faq.q: When does tuna season start in Marbella?
faq.a: The bluefin tuna season in Marbella typically begins in June and runs through October. The peak period is August, when water temperatures reach 25°C and tuna are most active. Some charter operators offer trips as early as May, but June is when the catch rates become reliable.

faq.q: What is the best month for tuna fishing in Marbella?
faq.a: August is widely considered the best month for bluefin tuna fishing in Marbella. Sea temperatures are high, tuna are feeding aggressively, and the weather is stable with light winds. September also offers excellent fishing with fewer crowds.

data.body_html:
Marbella's 2044 tuna season promises world-class bluefin fishing just minutes from Puerto Banús. Whether you're a seasoned angler or a first-timer, knowing the best months and tips will maximise your catch. This guide covers everything: season timing, boat recommendations, and what to expect from a Marbella fishing charter.

When Is Tuna Season in Marbella?

The bluefin tuna season runs from June to October, with the peak in August. Sea temperatures rise to 25°C, triggering feeding frenzies. Early-season trips in June offer fewer crowds, while September provides stable weather and still-active fish. Avoid November through May, when tuna migrate elsewhere.

Best Boats for Tuna Fishing from Puerto Banús

For offshore tuna, you need a boat that's fast, stable, and spacious. Our fleet includes two ideal options:

  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – €4,719 for 4 hours, includes a free jet ski. Cruises at 25 knots, reaching fishing grounds in under 45 minutes.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – Pricing on request via WhatsApp. Comfortable flybridge for spotting fish.

Both depart from Puerto Banús and come with a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. For smaller groups, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) is a nimble alternative.

What to Expect on a Tuna Charter

Your day starts at Puerto Banús marina. After a safety briefing, you'll head 5–15 nautical miles offshore. The skipper uses sonar and local knowledge to locate schools. Tuna fishing is active: you'll use heavy rods, reels, and live bait or lures. Expect to fight fish averaging 30–70 kg. All gear is provided; just bring sunscreen, a hat, and a camera.

Tips for a Successful Tuna Trip

  • Book early – August weekends fill by May. Secure your spot via WhatsApp.
  • Choose a morning charter – Tuna feed more aggressively at dawn. Depart at 8:00 AM.
  • Dress for the sun – Marbella averages 330 sunny days a year. UV is strong even in September.
  • Bring seasickness tablets – Even on a 24m Mangusta, offshore swells can affect some.
  • Practice catch-and-release – Helps sustain the bluefin population for future seasons.
